hook.en: Gold, silver and bronze to three of eight runners: swapping two winners gives a different result. Counting such ordered choices is a permutation.

say.en: Gold, silver and bronze to three of eight runners: swapping two winners gives a different result. Counting such ordered choices is a permutation. In this lesson: Use factorial notation.

body.en: $n! = 1 \times 2 \times 3 \times \cdots \times n$, and $0! = 1$. So $n! = n \times (n-1)!$: for example $7! = 7 \times 6 \times 5!$, which makes ratios such as $7!/5! = 42$ quick.

body.en: A permutation is an arrangement in a definite order. The number of *permutations* of $n$ different objects taken $r$ at a time, without repetition, is ${}^nP_r = \dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!}$. All $n$ at a time: ${}^nP_n = n!$. With repetition allowed: $n^r$.
body.kn: n ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ವಸ್ತುಗಳಿಂದ r ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ಕ್ರಮವಾಗಿ ಜೋಡಿಸುವ ರೀತಿಗಳು ⁿPᵣ = n!/(n − r)!.

narration.en: n P r counts ordered arrangements of r objects chosen from n different ones. It equals n factorial divided by n minus r factorial.
narration.kn: n ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ವಸ್ತುಗಳಿಂದ r ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ಕ್ರಮವಾಗಿ ಜೋಡಿಸುವ ರೀತಿಗಳು ⁿPᵣ = n!/(n − r)!.

say.en: n P r counts ordered arrangements of r objects chosen from n different ones. It equals n factorial divided by n minus r factorial. to the power nP r equals nn minus 1...(n - r plus 1): r factors.
say.kn: n ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ವಸ್ತುಗಳಿಂದ r ವಸ್ತುಗಳನ್ನು ಕ್ರಮವಾಗಿ ಜೋಡಿಸುವ ರೀತಿಗಳು to the power nP r equals n!/(n - r)!.

say.en: With repetition: n to the power r.

nn minus 1n minus 2n minus 3 equals 20 nn minus 1.
Cancel nn minus 1: n minus 2n minus 3 equals 20 equals 5 times 4.
n minus 2 equals 5, so n equals 7.
So the answer is n equals 7.

to the power 9P 4 equals 9 times 8 times 7 times 6 equals 3024.
So the answer is 3024.
